Owner Takes Her 1955 Chevy Bel Air to a Custom Car Shop, Goes Home in an EV
27 photos
Photo: West Coast Customs | Instagram
A longtime client called the CEO of a custom car shop one day. He told him he wanted to convert his entire car collection into EVs, and his 1955 Chevy Bel Air would be the first to undergo the conversion. Months later, he went home in a Bel Air that she could plug in at any Supercharger.
Troy Swope, an entrepreneur Troy Swope, called Ryan Friedlinghaus, the CEO and founder of West Coast Customs, and told him he had big plans with all the cars in her garage. West Coast Customs once swapped the original engines of those vehicles for more powerful plants. Now, out go the powerful plants, and in goes an electric motor.
She also brought in a Tesla Model 3 for the team, so the project started by chopping the body off the EV and stripping it down to bare chassis to build a functional electric platform to fit the classic Bel Air. This is how they ended up with what was basically a rolling skateboard, and then, they put the Bel Air on top of it.
West Coast Customs is known for swapping original engines for more powerful powerplants. They have done it with old Mustang bodies on top of new Mustang platforms. They have done the same with Camaros and GTOs.
Photo: West Coast Customs | Instagram But planting an old Chevy Bel Air on top of a Tesla Model 3 is a whole different story. " The whole process was tedious ," Ryan Friedlinghaus sums up the whole process of chopping, welding, chopping again. What came out of their “laboratory” is the Project B-Zero.
Instead of riding on the Tesla stock setup, the Chevy Bel Air features a custom-engineered air ride suspension, which allows the 20-inch custom wheels to tuck seamlessly into the fenders when it is aired out and the car rides low.
Troy wanted the Chevy to look every inch a stock Bel Air. So that is exactly what West Coast Customs did. He also asked for a modern twist, so the old two-tone white and red vanished under a matte Cherry Satin Red.
High-contrast Gloss Black trim replaced traditional chrome elements, modernizing the vehicle's appearance while preserving the 1955 silhouette . The car now features updated LED headlights and custom taillights integrated directly into the vintage body panels.
Photo: West Coast Customs | Instagram Pop the door, and you have access to a complete Tesla interior, but with a twist. The cabin has been reimagined with black suede, white stitching, and red accents. The seating and trim panels feature a distinct custom Hex/Octagon stitched pattern, instead of the usual diamond, using premium leather and Alcantara.
The custom dashboard integrates the minimalist Tesla control layout, including the touchscreen with the original interface. The three-spoke steering wheel is also from the Model 3, bearing the Tesla logo in the center, while the custom trunk is an extension of the cabin.
The Tesla underneath remains fully functional. It retains the safety features and the tech, including Autopilot and self-park capabilities. And it looks like it is going to be a company car. Lisa Evans, sales and integrated marketing executive who handles Business Development for Terramtech, Troy Swope’s company, shows up on camera as the owner of the vehicle to say how "so easy to drive" the electric Bel Air is.
West Coast Customs hasn’t disclosed the output of its all-new Project B-Zero, but since they said “motor,” not "motors," we should rule out the dual-motor variants. So we’re left with the base 279 horsepower (283 metric horsepower) variant, which does 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 5.8 seconds, and the 260-horsepower (264 metric horsepower) Model 3 setup, which can normally do 0 to 60 in 4.9 seconds.
Photo: West Coast Customs | Instagram There is no word about the battery pack this vintage-looking EV got, but the single-motor Model 3 comes with two battery options. The base version gets a 64-kWh unit, which stores enough energy for a drive of up to 272 miles (438 kilometers) before the car needs to be plugged in again. Then, there is the 82.0-kWh battery pack, fitted in the Model 3 Long Range, which is good for 363 miles (584 kilometers). Sure, those figures must have changed with the conversion.
Troy or whoever drives this car can plug the 1955 Chevy Bel Air right in at a Supercharger. Hopefully, nobody will call the police for ICEing. Many U.S. states and cities have specific laws prohibiting gas-powered vehicles from blocking EV chargers.
Fines vary by location, ranging from around $25 to over $350. Furthermore, Troy Swope, Lisa Evans, or any driver, for that matter, could have the car towed away if the police fail to notice that the good, old Chevy is actually a Tesla underneath and is there for no other purpose than charging.
However, the 71-year-old Bel Air shouldn't expect others to respect its elders and will wait in line for its turn and enjoy the second lease on life that it got, while many of its siblings rot in junkyards or barns.

European 1974 Pontiac Firebird Returns to America With 19K Miles, Minor Restoration Needed
16 photos
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1
This Pontiac Firebird isn’t just a car needing a minor restoration. It’s more than that. It’s a specimen that could easily become a collectible, coming directly from Europe to find a new home in the United States.
The vehicle landed on eBay without many specifics about its past, and that’s quite a shame. We don’t know how it ended up on the Old Continent and why it is now trying to get back to the States. But what we do know is something truly fantastic for diehard Pontiac fans: this is a low-mile car, with the odometer showing only 32,000 kilometers, which should mean less than 20,000 miles.
The Firebird was still a popular choice in 1974, despite the Trans Am getting more and more traction in the American car market.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 The 1974 Firebird production came down to 73,729 cars, and the base Firebird accounted for most cars with 26,372 orders. This made sense, considering it was also the most affordable car in the entire lineup. This happened at a time when cars with big power under the hood struggled, and the GTO knows this very well.
The Esprit was the runner-up in terms of sales with 22,583 cars, while the Formula was still more popular than the Trans Am - despite this not lasting much more - with 14,519 orders. The Trans Am was fourth in the charts with 10,255 units.
Pontiac was one of the few companies that were still betting big on large displacement, and the Trans Am was the living proof that American buyers still wanted more power. Trans Am sales went up from 4,802 units, so they more than doubled.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 The Trans Am could be ordered with a 400 with either manual and automatic transmissions, a 455 available only with an automatic, and an SD 45 with both manual and automatic. The SD was the rarest choice, making its way to only 943 garages.
Most people bought the 400 and the 455, and the automatic transmission was the preferred choice.
This Firebird has a six-cylinder engine under the hood, and that’s not necessarily a problem. Paired with an automatic transmission, the base six offered on the Firebird in 1974 made perfect sense for people who wanted a daily driver.
The Firebird was an excellent choice for an efficient ride with an eye-catching design, and this six-cylinder configuration allowed buyers to enjoy this package without spending many dollars on gas and maintenance.
However, I wish we knew more about how the car ended up in Europe. It’s unclear if the car was sent to the Old Continent immediately after rolling off the assembly lines or someone bought it along the way, but it’s now trying to return to the United States.
We’re not seeing the odo, but considering the seller claims the mileage is in kilometers, this Firebird was probably destined for the European market from the very beginning.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 Its condition is impressive, and everything seems to suggest that the 19K miles on the clock are accurate. The car has probably been babied throughout its entire life, so it’s just a shame that we’re not being provided with more data about the previous ownership.
The interior looks complete, in good shape, and original, but I would still want to know more information about any previous repairs that it might have received. Considering the car is still in Europe, a live inspection is more difficult, so maybe a third-party professional verification is the right approach.
The seller describes this car as a great base for restoration projects, but at first glance, it doesn’t require major work to return to its original glory days. For example, the rust damage doesn’t seem to cause major concerns, so if possible, call the seller and maybe ask for more detailed photos - especially in good light - that expose the underside. It’s also unknown if the car still has the original metal on the floors and the rest of the body.
Photo: eBay seller Consignify1 This is a six-cylinder Firebird, and this is often a reason for many potential buyers to walk away. We all know that most collectors are into V8 power, so if you believe that a six is not worth your money, maybe the fact that this car was exported to Europe is a more important selling point.
The car is currently located in Belgium, but it’s unclear if this is the place where it shipped after waving goodbye to the United States. The seller believes that $24,800 is a fair price, but considering the car is now located in Europe, you should also consider the shipping costs back to the United States.
The Make Offer option has also been enabled, and the dealer says the car is ready for export, meaning that you shouldn’t spend much time to get the necessary papers to bring the Firebird back home.
